headline: Bangladesh crushes Australia by nine wickets for first-ever Test win on Australian soil
summary: The Tigers made history in Darwin, becoming the quickest Asian team to win a Test in Australia, achieving the feat in just their third attempt Down Under.
details: Bangladesh made history in Darwin, crushing Australia by nine wickets on Sunday for their first-ever Test win on Australian soil. The Tigers needed just 57 runs and wrapped up proceedings in the second session on Day 4 against a full-strength Australian side.

Bangladesh is now the quickest Asian team to win a Test in Australia, achieving this feat in their third Test Down Under. This record surpasses Pakistan (7 Tests) and India (12 Tests), while Sri Lanka remains winless after 15 attempts.

The nine-wicket victory marks Bangladesh's second-biggest Test win by wickets, following their 10-wicket triumph over Pakistan in Rawalpindi in 2024. It is also only their second win against Australia in seven Tests, with the first being in Mirpur in 2017.

Australia's loss at home to an Asian team other than India is the first in 31 years, a streak that dates back to 1995. This historic win also marks Bangladesh's second Test victory in SENA countries, complementing their famous win against New Zealand in Mount Maunganui in 2022.

Hasan Mahmud's match figures of 9-111 are the second-best by a Bangladesh pacer in Tests, only behind Shahadat Hossain's 9-97 in 2008. These figures are also the best by a Bangladesh bowler outside the country, surpassing Mehidy Hasan Miraz's 9-148 in 2021.

Furthermore, Hasan's 9-111 are the third-best match figures by a visiting bowler in their debut Test in Australia. Only England's Maurice Tate (1924) and Pakistan's Wasim Akram (1990) have taken more wickets with 11 each.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto recorded his third away Test win, the most by any Bangladesh captain, surpassing Mominul Haque and Mushfiqur Rahim who had two each. Shanto also holds the overall record for most Test wins as Bangladesh captain, with nine victories.
The Darwin Test saw a record attendance of 18,352 fans, the highest ever at the venue. This enthusiastic support underscored the significance of Bangladesh's historic achievement.

headline: PM urges vigilance against 'confusion-makers', citing past actions and future intentions
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman called on citizens to be wary of those spreading misinformation, emphasizing the need to scrutinize their past and future actions. He made these remarks during a family card distribution and honorarium event in Kishoreganj.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged the public to be cautious of 'confusion-makers' and rumour-mongers in the country. He stressed the importance of observing their past actions and keeping a close eye on their future activities based on that history.

The Prime Minister made these statements on Sunday, August 16, while addressing a Family Card distribution and honorarium ceremony at the Old Kishoreganj Stadium. During the event, he distributed Family Cards to women, honorariums to imams, muezzins, priests, monks, and pastors, and financial aid checks to the underprivileged and disabled.

Criticizing the role of certain groups during various political crises, the Prime Minister highlighted their absence from democratic movements in the 1971 Liberation War, and political events in 1986, 1996, and the last 17 years. He noted that BNP and its allies' activists were the ones who faced disappearances, killings, torture, and oppression during the last 17 years of struggle.

Referring to recent discussions on 'reform', Tarique Rahman stated that those who were absent from the streets for 17 years are now spreading confusion with grand talks of reform. He reminded that BNP first presented a state reform roadmap to the public in 2022, and earlier, the first reform proposal in the country was formulated under Begum Khaleda Zia's leadership.

The Prime Minister outlined the government's public welfare priorities, including the effective implementation of Family Cards and Farmer Cards for social protection, providing allowances to imams and muezzins, and developing future generations as good citizens. He also reiterated the commitment to modernize the agricultural sector and establish new factories and industries to create employment for youth.

He emphasized that a country cannot progress by leaving its people behind or failing to prepare them properly. The Prime Minister stated that the government's main goal is to build an self-reliant and welfare-oriented Bangladesh, where every citizen receives due respect and support from the state according to their capacity.

Highlighting the empowerment of women, who constitute half of the population, the Prime Minister mentioned that groundbreaking initiatives like the Family Card have been adopted to make women self-reliant and empowered. This aims to provide every family with a strong economic foundation, alongside free education for women up to graduation and government assistance for good results.

Regarding agriculture, the government has introduced Farmer Cards and waived agricultural loans up to 10,000 Taka, benefiting 1.3 million farmers. Future plans include excavating 250 kilometers of canals nationwide to improve irrigation and address water scarcity.

For education, the Prime Minister presented a new roadmap focusing on holistic development, including sports, cultural activities, and language skills, beyond institutional certificates. He also announced the reintroduction of the 'Notun Kuri' competition, originally launched by former President Ziaur Rahman, to foster talent.

He reaffirmed the government's commitment to the welfare of all segments of society, noting special social allowances for imams, muezzins, khatibs, and other religious leaders. Additionally, the current BNP government has resolved and disbursed retirement benefits for 123,000 teachers who suffered during the autocratic regime.
